raw_reply:
AppleMusic v85: CONDITIONAL PASS

What looks correct

Stage2 numbering appears confined to the expected broad AppleMusic regions: topbar, left navigation, and main content.

Main content cards are still present in the expected rows.

The first row 3.3?3.6 cards look structurally preserved.

The second row 3.8 / 3.9 / 3.10 / 3.11 cards are still inside the main content area.

Bottom partial cards remain inside the lower main-content section.

I do not see obvious new pollution from QQ/Python Stage1.5 rules.

Visible issues

3.12 remains an incomplete/review-only card. It is still not a clean full media card.

Topbar labels and control clusters are still visually dense.

Left-side review/background strip remains visually prominent, though it does not appear to leak into main content.

This is not a full Stage2 quality pass; it is only ?no obvious v85 regression.?

Regression vs expectation

No obvious regression from the stated AppleMusic protected baseline.

Expected broad primary usage is acceptable here because AppleMusic does not require Stage1.5 content-column replacement.

QQ v85: CONDITIONAL PASS

What looks correct

Broad primary does not appear to be used as one undifferentiated numbering target.

Numbered items are visibly grouped into the expected areas:

conversation list,

message thread,

bottom composer,

right sidebar,

top/header.

Conversation-list items stay in the left conversation pane.

Message/card/bubble items stay in the message thread.

Bottom toolbar/send items are in the bottom composer area.

Right-side notice/member items remain inside the right sidebar.

Visible issues

The message thread still has dense parent/child overlays; message/card/bubble layering is visually busy.

The bottom composer looks usable, but it should remain review-only; its exact semantic boundary still needs caution.

Right sidebar notice/member area remains cluttered.

Topbar is still dense and has several small controls close together.

Some message context labels and parent boxes still obscure content.

Regression vs expectation

No obvious regression from v80/v81 protected behavior.

The broad primary is not visibly being directly numbered, which is the key v85 requirement for QQ.

Still not a full pass because internal message structure remains noisy.

Python.org v85: CONDITIONAL PASS

What looks correct

Browser chrome is not visibly being numbered as main webpage content.

Website header/navigation/search remain separate from the page body.

Stage2 numbering appears concentrated in:

header/nav/search,

hero/content area,

cards/list/news/events inside the central content column.

I do not see broad right-side blank primary area being heavily numbered.

The right floating/scroll area remains visually separate/review-like.

Visible issues

The central content_column is still visually noisy; hero/code/text/card/list areas are heavily fragmented.

There are many dense orange boxes inside the hero and card/list sections.

Some blue structural/review boxes still overlap heavily in the main content area.

The left edge of the content column has a few questionable small candidates near blank/low-content areas; these should be checked against the content_column boundary.

News/events and lower cards still look structurally busy.

Regression vs expectation

No obvious regression against the v85 requirement that broad primary should not be directly numbered.

Visually, the numbering target appears to be the central content area, not the whole wide primary background.

Still only conditional because the internal webpage content structure is very dense and not clean.

Summary
AppleMusic v85: CONDITIONAL PASS
QQ v85: CONDITIONAL PASS
Python.org v85: CONDITIONAL PASS

No interface shows an obvious protected-set regression from the stated v85 dataflow change.

But none of these should be treated as a full Learning Mode pass. The main remaining issues are:

Python.org content column is still over-fragmented.

QQ message/thread internal structure is still noisy.

AppleMusic still has the known incomplete 3.12 card.

Topbar overlays remain dense across interfaces.

All outputs remain display/review-only, not execution or PathGraph promotion material.
